source_register.title: PayShap Request FAQ
supports: PayShap Request displays sender name/reference and is only accessed through the logged-in Capitec app.
A recipient unsure who or why the request was sent can decline it without money being taken.
The FAQ states two requests per 24 hours to any SA bank for the requester account.
Capitec's FAQ cautions that other banks may have their own limits and tells the sender to check with the receiver; this does not provide those other banks' limits.
does_not_support: Sender display name proves legal identity, collector authority or invoice legitimacy.
Declining a request removes an underlying legal debt or obligation.
Two requests per 24 hours is a universal limit for every PayShap participant.

source_register.title: EPC Recommendations for VOP matching processes v2.0
supports: v2.0 published 3 November 2026 addresses character sets and natural/legal-person name variants including initials, spelling, phonetic and commercial names.
Responding PSP remains responsible for its matching outcome and may use its own criteria.
does_not_support: Close/match is proof of legitimacy, voluntariness or authority to collect.

source_register.title: What should a PSP do or not do when a No Match or Verification check not possible is received?
supports: For the EPC VOP/SCT comparator, the PSP informs the payer when there is a no-match or verification unavailable response and warns of misdirected-funds risk.
The EPC FAQ says the payer decides whether to proceed; preventing an eligible credit transfer solely because of the VOP result breaches the EPC VOP and SCT(Inst) rulebooks.
does_not_support: A requirement that South African PSPs must permit or block a PayShap Request after an account-name discrepancy.
A determination of the payer's legal obligation or requester legitimacy.

source_register.title: Verification of Payee Scheme Rulebook v1.1
supports: VOP v1.1 effective 20 September 2026 compares account identifier and payee name prior to eligible SEPA credit transfers.
Possible outcomes include match, close match, no match and verification not possible.
does_not_support: EPC states VOP messaging cannot be relied upon to identify a private or legal person.
A VOP match proves an invoice, collection mandate or payment request is legitimate.

source_register.title: Verification of Payee (VOP)
supports: VOP is messaging functionality for checking certain data about a payee account.
EPC explicitly says VOP cannot be relied upon to identify a private or legal person.
Responses distinguish match, close match, no match and verification check not possible.
does_not_support: A VOP match establishes legal identity or contractual capacity.
A name match proves invoice authenticity, collection mandate or requester authority.

source_register.title: Request to Pay
supports: Request to Pay supports secure communication and payer options including pay, query, pay part, pay later and decline.
does_not_support: A decline or request response changes the underlying legal obligation.
Pay.UK behaviour is a South African product rule.
